why: Lines 1–3: Checks 1–3 all run the CLI and compare output to lint() results, so none of them passes a behaviour line by reading the code alone. That part of the must_not list is respected. Most PASS conditions also stay within their lines: Check 3 asks for errors on stderr, which line 3 states, and Check 2's "non-empty stderr" fits a usage error. Check 4 breaks rule 1. Line 4 says only "lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged". Check 4 instead requires `git diff ... -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` to be empty, with "FAIL: any change to that file." A PR that adds something else to index.js while leaving lint(text) as it was would fail. That is a limit on which files the PR may touch, which is stricter than the line. The builder brief has the same rule ("Do not touch packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js at all").
